question.text: A spherical balloon of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> containing helium gas has a pressure of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>48</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> bar. At the same temperature, the pressure, of a spherical balloon of radius<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> containing the same amount of gas will be<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>…</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></math> bar.

solution.text:
if volume of 3cm balloon is =V
then volume of 12cm radius balloon =64V
So pressure will become 1 / 64 times =1/64×48×10-3 bar =750×10-3 bar
